top3.why: The final session of an eight-part read-through of Ursula K. Le Guin's The Dispossessed — her 1974 anarchist-utopia novel, one of the genre's foundational political texts — closes out with the group landing on the book's ambiguous politics rather than just recapping plot. *(confirm details)*: the listing gives no address beyond "Philadelphia," so confirm the location before heading over.

Iffy Books keeps running some of the city's best hands-on DIY-electronics programming, and this one's a genuine mashup: hand-build a small clay sculpture with an NFC tag embedded inside that can trigger phone shortcuts when tapped. $4.86 covers the clay-and-tag kit; instruction is pay-what-you-can ($5-$15 suggested, notaflof). Center City/Fitler Square, an easy walk from Rittenhouse.

A talk marking the 150th anniversary of the Battle of Little Bighorn, reframing it through Native nations' own history and the broader fate of the American West — exactly the kind of indigenous-history programming that's easy to miss amid the museum's bigger exhibits. At the National Constitution Center in Old City, an easy walk from Center City.

annotations.note: A quantum physicist's machine that tunnels into a subatomic universe accidentally reveals a radical cancer treatment — 2024 sci-fi/horror, 82 minutes, watched together online by the Philadelphia Area Horror Meetup Group.

top3.why: Eastern State Penitentiary's lecture series turns its own history inside out this time, tracing a line from Philadelphia's founding "natural rights" rhetoric to the carceral state the city went on to help build — the kind of institution-critiquing public history that's easy to walk past. A one-off talk inside one of the city's most resonant sites for thinking about incarceration and state power. Fairmount — take the 48 bus or walk about 20 minutes from the Broad Street Line's Fairmount Ave stop.

Latrice Royale — a standout from RuPaul's Drag Race, by reputation — brings a holiday-themed send-up of White Christmas to City Winery for one night. Broad, campy, big-personality queer performance that's worth the ticket regardless of the room it's in. Center City, Chinatown.

A rare big-screen outing for Ninotchka, Ernst Lubitsch's 1939 comedy where Greta Garbo plays a stone-faced Soviet envoy who melts in gay Paris — witty, quietly political, and exactly the kind of repertory programming a commercial multiplex would never touch. Chestnut Hill — reachable via Regional Rail's Chestnut Hill East Line or the 23 bus up Germantown Ave.

annotations.note: Conor McPherson's acclaimed ghost-story play, by reputation — strangers trade supernatural tales in a rural Irish pub.
Hands-on Rust coding meetup — ownership and borrowing, building a first CLI, or working on your own project, with help on compiler errors and systems-programming questions.
Three 40-minute silent-writing sprints with 10-minute breaks and accountability check-ins; BYO coffee and laptop charger.
A toxic-gas leak at a medical supply warehouse raises hungry zombies from a nearby cemetery — 1985 horror-comedy classic, 95 minutes, watched together online for a member's birthday.

top3.why: Nocturne, which reads as a goth/industrial night that used to run regularly before it stopped, gets a one-off reunion with DJs Jon Gill, Kathy Fadigan, and Mike Saga spinning the old sets. 21+, 9pm-2am, $20 — a real chance to catch a scene that doesn't throw parties like this often anymore. Just north of the Convention Center at 13th & Callowhill, an easy walk from Jefferson Station or the Chinatown stop on the Broad-Ridge Spur.

What looks like an annual "Gothsgiving" tradition in Philly's goth scene: DJs Baby Berlin and Plaguelustre spinning death rock, post-punk, darkwave, and goth at The 700. 21+, 10pm-2am, $10 advance/$15 door. Northern Liberties, a few blocks from the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop or the 57 bus.

Vibraphonist Julian Lee leads his quartet for a Rittenhouse jazz-club set — low-key, chairs-and-cocktails jazz on a night most of the city is cooking or pre-gaming for Thanksgiving. Chris' Jazz Cafe is one of the city's few rooms still built around a stand-up jazz program, not a concept.

annotations.note: No cover — DJ EBGIII spinning darkwave, goth rock, '80s electro, and industrial, 8pm-midnight.
Low-key coding meetup — no panels or pitches, just coffee and focused time to build, learn, and connect, run in collaboration with Blockspace Community.
Hands-on session experimenting with VHS tapes and audio cassettes, with equipment on hand for analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog transfers.
A girl with unusual powers escapes a mental asylum and tries to make it on her own in New Orleans — 2021 fantasy/thriller, 106 minutes, watched together online by the Philly horror meetup.
Rated R, 111 min.
Rated R, 126 min.
Rated R, 115 min.
Rated PG-13, 131 min.
A college student alone on campus over Thanksgiving break is targeted by a group of outcasts and must fight back — 2014 horror/crime, 86 minutes, the Philly horror meetup's Thanksgiving pick.

top3.why: Three-band punk/rock bill at Silk City on Black Friday night — Leadpetal, The Angies, and Nadafinger, the kind of all-local DIY lineup that's easy to miss under the holiday-shopping noise. Spring Garden/Northern Liberties, a few blocks from the Market-Frankford Line's Spring Garden stop or the 57 bus.

A James Brown tribute happy hour — the archival/tribute-night sweet spot for soul, done as a dance party rather than a note-for-note cover band. The Trestle Inn in Callowhill, a few blocks from the Convention Center and Jefferson Station.

Chris Oatts leads a full big band through a set with guest vocalist Chelsea Reed at Chris' Jazz Cafe — one of the city's few rooms that still books a working big band on a regular night, not just for a holiday special. Center City, Rittenhouse.

annotations.note: Miami-based jazz vocalist, by reputation, for a multi-night run at SOUTH Jazz Club.
An Italian horror-fantasy (subtitled) about a haunted teacher who uncovers a village's dark healing ritual built around a teenage boy — 2025, 122 minutes.
Ben Vaughn is a Philadelphia-rooted singer-songwriter and producer, by reputation, here leading a quintet for WXPN's long-running free lunchtime concert series.

top3.why: Harriett's Bookshop — the Fishtown shop built around Black and women authors and named for Harriet Tubman — doesn't show up in Collection most weeks, so a rare appearance is worth taking. This is their Small Business Saturday trolley tour, moving shoppers between Black- and women-owned storefronts rather than steering foot traffic to the usual chains. Fishtown, near the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop or the 15 trolley on Girard Ave.

A five-band punk and power-pop bill at Vox Populi, the long-running artist-run collective space, by reputation — Dark Sufers come down from New Jersey to headline, backed by local openers Shampoo, Sappers, The Speed Dials, and TTLC. A few blocks north of the Convention Center, near the Broad-Ridge Spur's Chinatown stop or Jefferson Station.

A rare theatrical rerun of Paul Thomas Anderson's Licorice Pizza — his 1970s San Fernando Valley coming-of-age story, one of the sharpest and funniest things he's made — at the Philadelphia Film Society's Chestnut Street screen. The kind of repertory booking that disappears fast once a studio's licensing window closes. Center City, Chestnut Street.

annotations.note: Marcus Gilmore and David Virelles are major names on the current jazz scene, by reputation — part of Solar Myth's mentoring-series programming.
Casual pair-programming meetup comparing Claude Code and Codex on the same tasks — bring a laptop and a project or workflow to test, work in small groups, compare notes.
Open work session for Philly's DC215 hacking group to make progress together on an active CTF.
Three themed decks aboard the Moshulu — emo with DJ Sabrina, metal with DJ Dan von DOOM, goth in the indoor lounge with DJ Kathy Fadigan. 21+, 10pm-2am, $7.18+.
Back-to-back Cure and Smiths tribute sets — doors 6pm, show 7:30pm, $24+.
A deaf writer fighting a masked killer in silence (Hush, 2016) paired with a blind woman defending against home invaders (See For Me, 2021) — both horror leads built around a missing sense.

top3.why: PhilaMOCA screens Andrzej Żuławski's 1985 L'Amour Braque (Mad Love) — one of the wilder entries in the Polish director's hysterical, maximalist filmography — to celebrate critic Samm Deighan's new book on his work, with Deighan herself in the room. Doors/reception at 7, screening introduction at 7:30. Exactly the kind of specialist film-and-literature crossover that justifies PhilaMOCA's whole existence. $12, Callowhill, an easy walk from the Convention Center or Jefferson Station.

A jazz jam session at Ortlieb's raising money for Juntos, the South Kensington-based immigrant-rights and workers' organization — led by Corey Bernhard, with the usual Sunday-night Ortlieb's crowd of serious players sitting in. Real stakes behind a low-key night of music. Northern Liberties, near the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop or the 57 bus.

Blitzkid — a long-running horrorpunk duo, by reputation, in the Misfits/Samhain lineage — headlines at MilkBoy with The Gentlemen Ghosts and Fading Radiance opening. A rare bill that satisfies both the horror column and the punk column at once. Center City, Chestnut Street.

annotations.note: An indoor flea market and holiday bazaar run by Animal ACTivists of Philly, with a Krampus appearance — animal-rights activism and market shopping under one roof at the Rotunda.
Weekly group watch-along of Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 — this week is Episode 5.
